slides.title: Welcome to Python
slides.prompt: Python is a powerful, beginner-friendly programming language used by companies like Google, Netflix, and NASA.

slides.title: Talking to the Computer
slides.prompt: To make Python display something on the screen, we use a built-in instruction called print().

slides.title: Quick Check
slides.prompt: Which instruction is used to display output in Python?
slides.explanation: print() is the universal Python function for sending output to the console.

slides.title: Adding Text
slides.prompt: Inside the parentheses of print(), we place the text we want to display. In programming, text is called a String.

slides.title: The Golden Rule of Strings
slides.prompt: Strings MUST be surrounded by quotes. You can use double quotes ("") or single quotes (''), as long as they match.

slides.title: Spot the String
slides.prompt: Which of the following is a valid Python string?
slides.explanation: Strings must be wrapped in quotation marks so the computer knows it is reading text, not a command.

slides.title: Syntax Errors
slides.prompt: If you forget the quotes, Python will crash and throw a SyntaxError because it thinks you are trying to use a command that doesn't exist.
slides.codeSnippet: print(Hello)  # ❌ This will cause an error!

slides.title: Find the Bug
slides.prompt: Which of these lines of code will crash when you run it?
slides.explanation: Without quotes, Python tries to read 'Welcome' as a command instead of text.

slides.title: Order Matters
slides.prompt: Python reads code strictly from top to bottom, line by line. This is called sequential execution.

slides.title: Final Challenge
slides.prompt: If we run this code, what will be printed last?
slides.explanation: Python executes line by line. "Go!" is on the final line, so it prints last.
